# Adjudication Task — Chapter 275

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃275화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|‘순진하시네요.’
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|전날 들었던 그 한마디가 머릿속을 떠나질 않는다.
 10|
 11|침대 옆에 있는 간병인 의자에 앉아 분무를 뿌리는 가습기를 물끄러미 바라보다가, 문득 떠오른 생각을 내뱉었다.
 12|
 13|“아니, 순진한 게 아니지.”
 14|
 15|무림은 도산검림(刀山劍林)이라는 말이 어울리는 세계였다.
 16|
 17|피를 보는 건 예사요, 죽음은 일상이다. 힘이 곧 정의이며 살아남는 자가 승자였다.
 18|
 19|잔혹한 무림의 일면을 목격할 때마다 현대를 떠올렸다.
 20|
 21|체계적인 복지와 법률. 사람들의 윤리 의식. 무림과는 비교도 안 되게 뛰어난 문명을 이룩한 세상.
 22|
 23|하지만 틀렸다.
 24|
 25|“순진한 게 아니라 멍청했던 거야.”
 26|
 27|무림인은 허리춤에 검을 차지만 현대인은 소매에 비수를 감춘다.
 28|
 29|몬스터는 게이트 안에만 있는 것이 아니라 밖에도 있었다.
 30|
 31|좋은 옷과 선량한 이미지로 몸을 두르고 빌딩 숲을 호령하는 자들. 소매에 숨겨 둔 비수를 드러내기 시작한 그놈들이 바로 게이트 밖의 몬스터다.
 32|
 33|‘원명훈처럼.’
 34|
 35|그동안 너무 말랑하게 생각했다. 세상이 불공평하고 좆 같다는 걸 알고 있으면서도, 안일한 마음을 버리지 못했다.
 36|
 37|여긴 현대니까. 21세기의 민주주의 사회니까. 능력을 증명하기 위한 치열한 아귀다툼이 있을지언정 오늘 같은 일은 일어나지 않을 거라 생각했다.
 38|
 39|‘그 결과가 이거고.’
 40|
 41|잠든 임꺽정을 응시했다. 팔꿈치 아래로 절단된 양팔은 고위 힐러의 회복 마법과 상급 포션으로 치료를 끝냈다.
 42|
 43|일상생활에는 별로 무리가 없겠지만…… 헌터로서의 복귀는 장담하기 어렵다. 포션은 만능이 아니니까.
 44|
 45|‘어떤 새끼냐.’
 46|
 47|차갑게 식은 머릿속에 여러 생각이 헤엄쳤다.
 48|
 49|누가, 왜. 어떤 목적으로 블랙 헌터를 보낸 걸까.
 50|
 51|임꺽정의 팔을 자른 것은 이쯤에서 멈추라는 경고일수도, 시작을 알리는 신호탄일 수도 있다.
 52|
 53|‘어떤 의미였는지는 곧 알게 되겠지.’
 54|
 55|그때까지 넋 놓고 기다릴 생각은 없다.
 56|
 57|나도, 최 팀장도.
 58|
 59|“쉬고 계세요. 아저씨.”
 60|
 61|흐트러진 이불을 임꺽정에게 덮어 준 그때였다.
 62|
 63|우우웅.
 64|
 65|진동과 함께 어둠 속에서 스마트폰이 환하게 밝혀졌다.
 66|
 67|짤막한 문자 한 통. 발신인은 최 팀장이다.
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|〈 최 팀장님
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|최 팀장님
 76|
 77|길드 하우스로.
 78|
 79|
 80|
 81|* * *
 82|
 83|
 84|
 85|문자를 확인한 즉시 병원을 나섰다. 깊은 새벽, 모두가 퇴근한 길드 하우스에는 두 사람이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
 86|
 87|“아, 진태경 씨.”
 88|
 89|“어서 와.”
 90|
 91|최 팀장, 그리고 송송이다.
 92|
 93|당연히 있을 거라고 짐작했던 김 집사는 보이지 않았다.
 94|
 95|내 시선을 알아차린 최 팀장이 먼저 입을 열었다.
 96|
 97|“잠깐 자리를 비우셨습니다.”
 98|
 99|“그래요?”
100|
101|그림자처럼 최 팀장 곁을 지키던 김 집사가 없는 건 의외였지만, 지금은 그게 중요한 것이 아니다.
102|
103|나는 거두절미하고 본론부터 꺼내 들었다.
104|
105|“무슨 일입니까?”
106|
107|“말씀드리기 전에 커피라도 한 잔 드려야 하는데…… 우선 이것부터 보시죠.”
108|
109|커피잔 대신 최 팀장이 내민 것은 자신의 스마트폰이었다. 화면에는 국내 최대 포털 사이트가 띄워져 있었다.
110|
111|길쭉한 손가락이 인터넷 기사 창을 터치하자 각 카테고리로 나뉜 기사들이 주르륵 떴다.
112|
113|그중에서도 맨 윗줄에 올라와 있는 기사를 눈으로 훑었다.
114|
115|
116|
117|[대중이 불러온 유명세 앞에 무릎 꿇은 사법부. 공정성은 어디에?]
118|
119|[통합당 최고의원 윤서윤 의원, “개인의 섣부른 행동이 불러온 죽음. 원명훈은 법의 심판을 받았어야.” 강한 질타…….]
120|
121|[정당방위인가? 살인인가?]
122|
123|
124|
125|정치, 사회면을 장식한 기사. 이름만 적혀 있지 않을 뿐, 누구를 가리키는 것인지는 명백했다.
126|
127|“이거, 언제 올라온 겁니까?”
128|
129|“한 시간 전입니다. 그런데 벌써 조회수 10만에 댓글은 5천 개가 넘었네요.”
130|
131|“한 시간 전이면 새벽 네 시쯤인데.”
132|
133|“생각보다 네티즌들이 부지런한 모양입니다. 아니, 알바생이라고 해야 하나.”
134|
135|“재밌네요.”
136|
137|내 입가에 맺힌 웃음만큼이나 차갑게 식은 커피를 한 모금 마신 최 팀장이 말했다.
138|
139|“더 재미있는 기사도 있습니다.”
140|
141|“여기서 더?”
142|
143|“조금 더 내려 보세요. 태경 씨가 기대한 것 이상일 테니까.”
144|
145|최 팀장의 말은 사실이었다. 스크롤을 내리던 손가락이 나도 모르게 우뚝 멈췄다.
146|
147|나는 굵게 칠해진 기사 제목을 말없이 응시했다.
148|
149|
150|
151|[옛 직장 동료 K씨 단독 인터뷰 선공개. “유명 헌터 J는 추악한 인간.”]
152|
153|
154|
155|기사를 터치하자 3분 남짓한 선공개 인터뷰 영상이 떴다. 15초의 브랜드 화장품 광고 후, 화면을 가득 채운 것은 정장을 빼입은 배불뚝이 남성이었다.
156|
157|얼굴에 약간의 모자이크를 넣긴 했지만 한눈에 알아볼 수 있었다.
158|
159|“하.”
160|
161|중년인, 아니 ‘옛 직장 동료 K씨’의 정체를 깨닫자 헛웃음이 터져 나왔다.
162|
163|너무나도 익숙한 얼굴. 다시는 볼 일 없을 것으로 생각했던 인간이 그곳에 있었다.
164|
165|“이렇게 다시 볼 줄은 몰랐는데.”
166|
167|내 어깨 너머로 함께 스마트폰을 들여다보고 있던 송송이가 물었다.
168|
169|“정말 아는 사람이야?”
170|
171|“알지. 모를 수가 없지.”
172|
173|“이런 거지 같은 인터뷰를 할 정도면 사이는 당연히 나빴겠고.”
174|
175|“아니.”
176|
177|“그럼 혹시 친했어?”
178|
179|“그게 아니라…….”
180|
181|저 인간과 내 사이를 어떤 단어로 표현해야 하나. 나는 곰곰이 생각하다가 입을 열었다.
182|
183|“좆 같았지.”
184|
185|“아.”
186|
187|아무리 생각해도 저 말이 딱 어울린다.
188|
189|우리의 관계는 그 정도로 최악이었다. 지금까지 얽혔던 일들을 생각하면 칼부림 한 번 나지 않은 게 이상할 정도로.
190|
191|나는 못 본 사이 더 살이 오른 얼굴을 빤히 바라봤다.
192|
193|‘상식 씨. 오랜만이네.’
194|
195|김상식. 소풍 길드의 팀장.
196|
197|F급 헌터였던 시절, 길드장을 충동질해 나를 해고한 장본인이 바로 그였다.
198|
199|등급 재심사를 받기 위해 협회에 들렀을 때 마주친 것이 마지막이었는데…… 이렇게 다시 볼 줄이야.
200|
201|‘그 후에 길드에서 잘렸다고 들었는데.’
202|
203|능력은 부족하고 탐욕은 충만한 인간이 바로 김상식이다. 이름과는 달리 상식도 부족해서 온갖 병신 짓은 다 하고 다니다가 잘린 거고.
204|
205|워낙 소인배의 대명사 같은 인간이라 나를 향해 이를 부득부득 갈고 있었을 것은 분명했다.
206|
207|그러니까 이런 인터뷰까지 찍었겠지.
208|
209|‘무슨 개소리를 하나 들어나 보자.’
210|
211|때마침 영상에서는 기자의 질문이 시작되고 있었다.
212|
213|「최근 유명해진 헌터 J씨에 대해 하실 말씀이 있다고 들었는데요. 우선 전 직장 동료라는 것이 사실입니까?」
214|
215|김상식이 어울리지 않게 진지한 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
216|
217|「틀림없는 사실입니다. 진태…… 아니지, J의 직속 상사였으니까요.」
218|
219|「정확히는?」
220|
221|「제 팀원이었습니다. 2년 전 게이트 사고 후 제가 팀장을 맡게 됐죠. 올해 여름에 J에게 해고를 통보한 것도 접니다.」
222|
223|「저런. 이유가 있었습니까?」
224|
225|「이유야 한두 개가 아니죠.」
226|
227|그 후 김상식은 울분에 찬 목소리로 나를 해고한 이유에 대해 쏟아냈다.
228|
229|하나하나가 주옥 같은 개소리였지만, 기자와의 마지막 문답은 화룡점정이라고 할 만했다.
230|
231|「저는 취업 비리라는 부당한 누명을 쓰고 20년 넘게 몸담았던 길드에서 쫓겨났지만, J를 해고한 것은 어떠한 사익을 위해서도 아니었습니다.」
232|
233|「다른 이유가 있었다는 말씀입니까?」
234|
235|「예.」
236|
237|고작 3분짜리 선공개 영상을 푼 이유가 있었다. 김상식은 구국의 열사처럼 비장한 얼굴로 대미를 장식했다.
238|
239|「2년 전 변이 게이트 사고 당시, J는 팀원들을 몬스터의 먹잇감으로 던져 주고 도망쳐 나왔습니다. 살기 위해서라면 온갖 추악하고 더러운 짓을 서슴지 않는…….」
240|
241|이어지는 뒷말은 제대로 들리지도 않았다.
242|
243|나는 곧 인터뷰 풀 버전을 공개하겠다는 자막과 함께 영상이 끝난 후에도 말없이 한참을 응시했다.
244|
245|마치 이대로 바라보고 있으면 화면에서 김상식이 튀어나오기도 할 것처럼.
246|
247|무거운 침묵을 깨트린 건 최 팀장의 한마디였다.
248|
249|“어떠셨습니까?”
250|
251|아, 어떠냐고?
252|
253|글쎄. 뒤통수가 얼얼하고, 한편으로는 웃음도 나고. 아랫배가 부글부글 끓어오르는 게.
254|
255|“아주 재밌네요. 팀장님 말씀처럼.”
256|
257|“저도 처음 보고 웃었습니다. 인터뷰에 나오는 K씨, 아니 김상식이라는 분이 대충 어떤 인물인지 아니까요. 문제는…….”
258|
259|“대중들은 별로 재미없어할 거라는 거죠.”
260|
261|“바로 그겁니다.”
262|
263|벌써 댓글 창은 폭파 직전이다.
264|
265|어느새 만 개가 넘어가는 댓글은 일일이 볼 필요도 없었다. 가장 많은 추천 수를 받은 베스트 댓글이 눈에 들어왔다.
266|
267|
268|
269|(Best댓글) 내 이럴 줄 알았다. 다리 건너 듣고 설마 했는데, 언젠가 한 번 터질 것 같았음.
270|
271|
272|
273|그 다리가 무슨 다리고 터지긴 뭐가 터지냐.
274|
275|어떤 호로 새낀지는 몰라도 눈앞에 없어서 다행이다.
276|
277|있었다면 최소한 다음 찌라시는 황천 육교 건너에서 듣게 만들어 줬을 테니까.
278|
279|“이건 뭐. 더 볼 필요도 없을 것 같네.”
280|
281|헛웃음을 지으며 댓글 창을 닫았다.
282|
283|스마트폰을 건네받은 최 팀장이 느슨하게 팔짱을 끼며 입을 열었다.
284|
285|“조직적입니다. 처음부터 노리고 블랙 헌터를 보낸 게 확실해졌어요.”
286|
287|“비난 여론 조성하는 것도 그놈들이고.”
288|
289|“사람이란 생물이 그렇습니다. 한번 제대로 물타기를 시작하면 중심을 잡기가 쉽지 않죠.”
290|
291|“이 와중에 꺽정 아저씨가 습격당한 건 기사 한 줄 안 나왔을 거고.”
292|
293|“잘 아시는군요.”
294|
295|“모르면 병신이죠. 사건 맡은 수사팀 쪽에서는 무슨 말 없었습니까?”
296|
297|최 팀장이 작게 고개를 저었다.
298|
299|“설마 그쪽도 한통속?”
300|
301|“역시 외압이 있는 것 같습니다. CCTV 자료도 저쪽 손에 있고요.”
302|
303|“목격자들이 있다고 하지 않았어요?”
304|
305|“세 명 모두 연락 끊겼습니다.”
306|
307|그거 끝내주네.
308|
309|나도 모르는 사이 힘이 들어간 주먹에서 뼈 어긋나는 소리가 들렸다.
310|
311|“이거, 너무 작정하고 들어오네요.”
312|
313|“철저하게 고립시키겠다는 의도 같습니다. 김상식 씨 인터뷰 영상도 그렇고요.”
314|
315|찌라시나 팔아먹는 삼류 언론사와 인터뷰한 것이 아니다.
316|

[P79]
“Oh.”

[P80]
No matter how I looked at it, those words fit perfectly.

[P81]
Our relationship had been that terrible. Considering everything that had happened between us, it was almost strange that no one had ever pulled a knife.

[P82]
I stared at the face that had somehow grown even fatter since the last time I’d seen him.

[P83]
*Mr. Common Sense. Long time no see.*

[P84]
Kim Sangshik, Team Leader of the Sopung Guild.

[P85]
Back when I was an F-rank Hunter, he had been the one who goaded the Guild Master into firing me.

[P86]
The last time I’d seen him was when I ran into him at the Association while getting my Grade reassessed. And now, here he was again.

[P87]
*I heard he got fired from the Guild afterward.*

[P88]
Kim Sangshik was short on ability and overflowing with greed. Despite his name, he was short on common sense, too. He’d gone around doing every idiotic thing imaginable until the Guild finally fired him.

[P89]
He was the very definition of a petty little man, so there was no doubt he’d been grinding his teeth at the thought of me ever since.

[P90]
That was probably why he’d agreed to an interview like this.

[P91]
*Let’s hear what kind of bullshit he’s spouting.*

[P92]
Right on cue, the reporter began asking questions.

[P93]
“I hear you have something to say about the recently famous Hunter J. First, is it true that you were his former colleague?”

[P94]
Kim Sangshik nodded with an uncharacteristically serious expression.

[P95]
“That is absolutely true. I was Jin Tae… No, I was J’s direct supervisor.”

[P96]
“More specifically?”

[P97]
“He was on my team. I became team leader after the Gate accident two years ago. I was also the one who informed J of his dismissal this summer.”

[P98]
“Oh dear. Was there a reason?”

[P99]
“There wasn’t just one.”

[P100]
Kim Sangshik then launched into an indignant tirade about why he had fired me.

[P101]
Every word was pure, undiluted bullshit, but his final exchange with the reporter was the crowning touch.

[P102]
“I was falsely accused of employment corruption and driven out of the Guild where I had worked for more than twenty years. But I did not fire J for personal gain.”

[P103]
“Are you saying there was another reason?”

[P104]
“Yes.”

[P105]
Now I understood why they had released this three-minute preview. Kim Sangshik brought it to a dramatic close with the grim expression of a martyr sacrificing himself for his country.

[P106]
“During the mutated Gate accident two years ago, J threw his teammates to the monsters as bait and fled. He’s the kind of man who won’t hesitate to commit any vile, disgusting act to survive…”

[P107]
I barely heard what came after that.

[P108]
Even after the video ended with a caption promising that the full interview would be released soon, I continued staring silently at the screen.

[P109]
As if Kim Sangshik might leap out of it if I stared long enough.

[P110]
Team Leader Choi broke the heavy silence.

[P111]
“What did you think?”

[P112]
Ah, what did I think?

[P113]
Well. I felt like I’d been clubbed in the back of the head, but part of me wanted to laugh. At the same time, something was boiling in my gut.

[P114]
“Very interesting. Just like you said, Team Leader.”

[P115]
“I laughed when I first saw it, too. I have a rough idea of what K—or rather, Kim Sangshik—is like. The problem is…”

[P116]
“The public won’t find it very funny.”

[P117]
“Exactly.”

[P118]
The comments section was already on the verge of exploding.

[P119]
There were more than ten thousand comments now, and I didn’t need to read them all. The most upvoted comment caught my eye.

[P120]
> **(Best comment)** I knew it. I heard it through the grapevine and thought, *No way,* but I always had a feeling this would blow up someday.

[P121]
*What vine? And what the hell is supposed to blow up?*

[P122]
I didn’t know what kind of asshole had written it, but he was lucky he wasn’t standing in front of me.

[P123]
If he had been, I would’ve made sure he heard the next piece of gossip from across the overpass to the Yellow Springs.

[P124]
“Well, I don’t think there’s any need to read more.”

[P125]
I closed the comments with a hollow laugh.

[P126]
Team Leader Choi took back his smartphone, loosely folded his arms, and spoke.

[P127]
“This is organized. It’s clear now that they planned to send the Black Hunters from the very beginning.”

[P128]
“And they’re the ones stirring up public outrage, too.”

[P129]
“That’s how people are. Once someone starts muddying the waters in earnest, it’s hard to keep your bearings.”

[P130]
“And I doubt there’ll be so much as a single line in the news about Uncle Kkeokjeong being attacked.”

[P131]
“You understand the situation well.”

[P132]
“If I didn’t, I’d be a fucking idiot. Has the investigation team handling the case said anything?”

[P133]
Team Leader Choi shook his head slightly.

[P134]
“Don’t tell me they’re in on it, too.”

[P135]
“There appears to be outside pressure. The CCTV footage is already in the other side’s hands.”

[P136]
“Didn’t you say there were witnesses?”

[P137]
“We’ve lost contact with all three.”

[P138]
“That’s just fantastic.”

[P139]
My fist clenched without me realizing it, and my knuckles cracked.

[P140]
“They’ve planned this down to the last detail.”

[P141]
“They seem intent on isolating you completely. The interview with Mr. Kim Sangshik is part of that.”

[P142]
We weren’t dealing with some Third Rate media company that made its money selling gossip.

[P143]
This was one of the country’s ten largest media outlets.

[P144]
They would wrap even the most ludicrous bullshit in glossy packaging and present it as credible. Then they would use money and power to lend it even more weight.

[P145]
For example… testimony from people who knew me well.

[P146]
“Looks like I’ll get to see my old coworkers again. Though I guess they’ll be hard to recognize once their faces are pixelated.”

[P147]
Team Leader Choi was looking at me strangely.

[P148]
“Why are you looking at me like that?”

[P149]
“As I recall, you had a good reputation within the Sopung Guild.”

[P150]
“I got along with everyone. It was such a dinky little Guild.”

[P151]
“Then why would you expect them to turn on you?”

[P152]
“Because there’s one thing that works on just about everyone. This. You know.”

[P153]
I brought my thumb and index finger together and rubbed them.

[P154]
In the end, it all came down to cash. Money was everything.

[P155]
And for Hunters who risked their lives to make money, the temptation would be even stronger.

[P156]
“Maybe it’s because I’ve been stabbed in the back so many times in a row, but… these are people I spent seven years laughing and joking around with, and I still can’t trust them.”

[P157]
A few days ago, I might have naively believed in my old coworkers.

[P158]
But not anymore. The world where dreams, friendship, and common sense meant anything had already vanished from my mind.

[P159]
“Judging by those articles in the politics and society sections, it looks like they’ve greased some lawmaker’s palm, too. You think they couldn’t buy off a few low-rank Hunters struggling to make ends meet?”

[P160]
“…”

[P161]
“It’s obvious. I’ll become the most despicable bastard alive and get torn to pieces online. The reputation I’ve built will come crashing down, and our Guild will come crashing down with it.”

[P162]
Team Leader Choi, who had been wearing that strange expression the entire time, let out a quiet laugh.

[P163]
“You’ve improved a little. You’re finally capable of thinking like a jaded adult.”

[P164]
“Are you taking back what you said yesterday about me being naive?”

[P165]
“I’ll decide after I see what you do from here.”

[P166]
“What?”

[P167]
“We can’t just stand by and let them do this to us.”

[P168]
As he spoke, he tapped his smartphone screen. The phone rang, and someone answered.

[P169]
“I found it. The tail.”

[P170]
Butler Kim’s low, smooth voice flowed from the speaker.

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 275

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃275화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|‘순진하시네요.’
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|전날 들었던 그 한마디가 머릿속을 떠나질 않는다.
 10|
 11|침대 옆에 있는 간병인 의자에 앉아 분무를 뿌리는 가습기를 물끄러미 바라보다가, 문득 떠오른 생각을 내뱉었다.
 12|
 13|“아니, 순진한 게 아니지.”
 14|
 15|무림은 도산검림(刀山劍林)이라는 말이 어울리는 세계였다.
 16|
 17|피를 보는 건 예사요, 죽음은 일상이다. 힘이 곧 정의이며 살아남는 자가 승자였다.
 18|
 19|잔혹한 무림의 일면을 목격할 때마다 현대를 떠올렸다.
 20|
 21|체계적인 복지와 법률. 사람들의 윤리 의식. 무림과는 비교도 안 되게 뛰어난 문명을 이룩한 세상.
 22|
 23|하지만 틀렸다.
 24|
 25|“순진한 게 아니라 멍청했던 거야.”
 26|
 27|무림인은 허리춤에 검을 차지만 현대인은 소매에 비수를 감춘다.
 28|
 29|몬스터는 게이트 안에만 있는 것이 아니라 밖에도 있었다.
 30|
 31|좋은 옷과 선량한 이미지로 몸을 두르고 빌딩 숲을 호령하는 자들. 소매에 숨겨 둔 비수를 드러내기 시작한 그놈들이 바로 게이트 밖의 몬스터다.
 32|
 33|‘원명훈처럼.’
 34|
 35|그동안 너무 말랑하게 생각했다. 세상이 불공평하고 좆 같다는 걸 알고 있으면서도, 안일한 마음을 버리지 못했다.
 36|
 37|여긴 현대니까. 21세기의 민주주의 사회니까. 능력을 증명하기 위한 치열한 아귀다툼이 있을지언정 오늘 같은 일은 일어나지 않을 거라 생각했다.
 38|
 39|‘그 결과가 이거고.’
 40|
 41|잠든 임꺽정을 응시했다. 팔꿈치 아래로 절단된 양팔은 고위 힐러의 회복 마법과 상급 포션으로 치료를 끝냈다.
 42|
 43|일상생활에는 별로 무리가 없겠지만…… 헌터로서의 복귀는 장담하기 어렵다. 포션은 만능이 아니니까.
 44|
 45|‘어떤 새끼냐.’
 46|
 47|차갑게 식은 머릿속에 여러 생각이 헤엄쳤다.
 48|
 49|누가, 왜. 어떤 목적으로 블랙 헌터를 보낸 걸까.
 50|
 51|임꺽정의 팔을 자른 것은 이쯤에서 멈추라는 경고일수도, 시작을 알리는 신호탄일 수도 있다.
 52|
 53|‘어떤 의미였는지는 곧 알게 되겠지.’
 54|
 55|그때까지 넋 놓고 기다릴 생각은 없다.
 56|
 57|나도, 최 팀장도.
 58|
 59|“쉬고 계세요. 아저씨.”
 60|
 61|흐트러진 이불을 임꺽정에게 덮어 준 그때였다.
 62|
 63|우우웅.
 64|
 65|진동과 함께 어둠 속에서 스마트폰이 환하게 밝혀졌다.
 66|
 67|짤막한 문자 한 통. 발신인은 최 팀장이다.
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|〈 최 팀장님
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|최 팀장님
 76|
 77|길드 하우스로.
 78|
 79|
 80|
 81|* * *
 82|
 83|
 84|
 85|문자를 확인한 즉시 병원을 나섰다. 깊은 새벽, 모두가 퇴근한 길드 하우스에는 두 사람이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
 86|
 87|“아, 진태경 씨.”
 88|
 89|“어서 와.”
 90|
 91|최 팀장, 그리고 송송이다.
 92|
 93|당연히 있을 거라고 짐작했던 김 집사는 보이지 않았다.
 94|
 95|내 시선을 알아차린 최 팀장이 먼저 입을 열었다.
 96|
 97|“잠깐 자리를 비우셨습니다.”
 98|
 99|“그래요?”
100|
101|그림자처럼 최 팀장 곁을 지키던 김 집사가 없는 건 의외였지만, 지금은 그게 중요한 것이 아니다.
102|
103|나는 거두절미하고 본론부터 꺼내 들었다.
104|
105|“무슨 일입니까?”
106|
107|“말씀드리기 전에 커피라도 한 잔 드려야 하는데…… 우선 이것부터 보시죠.”
108|
109|커피잔 대신 최 팀장이 내민 것은 자신의 스마트폰이었다. 화면에는 국내 최대 포털 사이트가 띄워져 있었다.
110|
111|길쭉한 손가락이 인터넷 기사 창을 터치하자 각 카테고리로 나뉜 기사들이 주르륵 떴다.
112|
113|그중에서도 맨 윗줄에 올라와 있는 기사를 눈으로 훑었다.
114|
115|
116|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
